learning: If line loss falls below 1.0 and s-bend progress exceeds 0.210, the wider coverage edge was helping and iteration 4's drop was the gain. If line loss stays at 1.0 or more, test the 12 mm footprint at ±0.04 m next. If the score drops well below 69 with the same controller, the wider row's shallower slope is the likely cause, and kp should rise before the row is changed back.
notes: Isolating test of the ±0.04 m, 16 mm row at the restored kp 1.2 / kd 0.4 / base_speed 1.1 controller. Compare directly against iteration 3 (69.46), since only the row changes.
rationale: Evidence: the best raced design is the ±0.03 m row at 16 mm, y = 0.04, with kp 1.2, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.1 (iteration 3, 69.46, reproduced exactly in iterations 5, 6 and 7). Every track ends off track at max error about 0.062 m, and line loss stays at 1.0 to 1.1 events per run. Iteration 4 changed the row to ±0.04 m and kp to 1.0 in the same race, and its score fell to 61.49 with progress down on the s-bend (0.210 to 0.160) and oval (0.184 to 0.170). That race cannot say which change caused the drop. The Builder's intent this iteration is the isolating test: ±0.04 m at 16 mm with the restored kp 1.2 / kd 0.4 controller. I am keeping every controller value at the iteration 3 setting, so any difference from 69.46 comes from the row. The weights stay at (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1). With the wider row the steering slope per metre falls, so kp 1.2 may give somewhat softer steering than iteration 3. I am not raising kp now, because that would confound the test. If line loss stays at 1.0 or more, the next step is a 12 mm footprint at ±0.04 m, not a gain change. Expected result: line loss below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and oval, and s-bend progress above 0.210. I make no claim about completion. The progress at first line loss is not an allowed measurement name, so I cannot request it directly.
